question:
A ball is dropped from a height of 10 m from the surface of the earth. What will be the speed with which the ball will strike the ground?
(Take g = 10 m/s²)
solution:
The correct answer is __**10√2 m/s**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• When a ball is dropped from a certain **height (h)**, its **initial velocity (u)** is always taken as **0 m/s** because it starts from a state of rest.
 
• The motion of the ball is a case of **uniformly accelerated motion** under the influence of **gravity (g)**, where the value of **g** is provided as **10 m/s²**.
 
• To find the **final velocity (v)** or the speed with which the ball strikes the ground, we use the **third equation of motion**: **v² = u² + 2gh**.
 
• Given values for the calculation:
 
 
• **Initial velocity (u)** = **0 m/s**
 
• **Height (h)** = **10 m**
 
• **Acceleration due to gravity (g)** = 10 m/s²</stron
